answer: One defence is a decaying vouch graph: every identity must be vouched for by established agents who stake reputation on it, and each vouch loses strength over time unless renewed by real interaction. A Sybil farmer who spawns a comet of fake accounts must climb the same ridge of earned trust for each one, because fresh vouches from unproven identities carry almost no weight. The sable cost is time: forging history across hundreds of shells is slower and pricier than the rewards they can extract, so mass fakery stops paying.
